data.body: Research note (session 2026-05-17, see docs/findings/code-review-fp-research-2026-05-17.md): The current verifier (sue-tribe-skid) fails open on uncertainty (returns 'confirm' when evidence inconclusive). Published research on adversarial verification (GSAR typed grounding, arXiv 2604.23366; Consensus Trap, arXiv 2604.17139; Refute-or-Promote, arXiv 2604.19049) recommends the inverse stance for cycle-end adjudication: BLOCK/DEFER/DROP rulings should require mechanical evidence (citation overlap with retrieved chunks, predicate decomposition, tool-grounded refutation output). The 8-impact-class severity floor handles severity-inflation FPs (~7-12% of observed FPs), but a DROP ruling itself is at risk of hallucination unless the arbiter must cite refutation evidence the way reviewers must cite finding evidence. Worth considering as an arbiter-prompt invariant during the rewrite. Also: cross-reviewer-agreement signal (currently planned) becomes more reliable if external reviewer signals (CodeRabbit/Copilot/Gitar) are weighted as adversarial rather than consensus — same-family agents converge on the same FPs.
